facts.fact: The deck says Malawi issues federated digital identities, with about 97% registration by November 2017 and 100% of the adult population by 2025.
The deck says the financial sector adopted NRB-issued identities as the primary identification and verifies customers through API-based eKYC against the national digital identity system.
The deck says banks and payment providers (eKYC), MACRA (SIM registration) and social protection programmes (beneficiary verification) rely on the NRB identity system.
The deck lists the Payment Systems Act, 2022 (a revision of the 2011 act) and the E-Money Regulation, 2019 among the supporting legal frameworks.

facts.fact: The deck says mobile money operators take part in the national instant payment system and that 7.23 million adults used mobile money in 2023.
The deck says the national switch gives account-to-account, wallet-to-wallet, account-to-wallet and wallet-to-account instant payments across banks and mobile money operators.
The deck says National Switch Limited is the digital public infrastructure integrating all commercial banks, mobile money operators, MFIs, SACCOs and fintechs for instant payments.
